desk.headline: Record sales up 11% to $1.44bn and EPS of $3.82, both above estimates; full-year sales and EPS outlook raised

other.label: Operating margin
other.change: vs 12.0% a year ago; incl. ~1.5 pts tariff refunds

other.label: Share buybacks (year to date)
other.change: 9% of shares at start of year

results: Sales rose 11% to a third-quarter record of $1.44bn with comparable sales up 6%, beating the $1.37bn estimate.
EPS jumped 62% to $3.82, above the $3.09 estimate; about $0.40 of that came from refunds of earlier US tariffs.
Both brands grew: Abercrombie +12% and Hollister +11%; every region grew double digits, led by APAC at +24%.
Fewer promotions pushed average selling prices higher, lifting operating margin to 15.5% from 12.0%.
The company bought back $100m of shares in the quarter ($382m this year) and held $724m of cash with no borrowings.

guidance.summary: Full-year outlook raised: sales growth now about 6% (was about 5%) and EPS of $13.70–13.90 (was $13.10–13.60); operating margin range unchanged. For Q4 it expects sales up about 7% and EPS of $4.40–4.60.

points: Management said customer traffic was stable and November started strongly heading into the holidays.
Average selling prices rose high single digits in Q3 on lower discounting; management expects mid-single-digit growth for the full year.
No more US tariff refunds are expected after the $120m booked in Q2 and Q3, which add about $2.15 to full-year EPS.
Freight is the main cost pressure, about 1 point worse in Q4 than planned in August, and management is not assuming relief in 2027.
Management flagged a possibly more promotional holiday and higher 2027 costs, with 2027 margin guidance due in March.
call.source: Call coverage: Investing.com transcript, 24 Nov 2026; GuruFocus via Yahoo Finance, 24 Nov 2026

watch: Holiday-quarter sales against the roughly 7% growth outlook, without further tariff-refund help.
Freight costs and whether higher selling prices hold if the market turns more promotional.
The 2027 margin outlook in March, after this year's one-off refund boost.
